title: Motor system inefficiency as an activity-dependent amplifier of fatigue in multiple sclerosis
title_zh: 运动系统低效作为多发性硬化症中活动依赖性疲劳放大器
abstract: Abstract Multiple sclerosis (MS) fatigue is clinically obvious but mechanistically elusive. It can dominate daily life despite modest disability, stable structural MRI findings, or preserved strength on examination. This Update reviews evidence that an important component of MS fatigue may arise from increased motor-control cost and incomplete recovery after activity. Voluntary muscle activation studies show that some people with MS have incomplete central access to available force, particularly after exertion. Functional imaging studies indicate that apparently preserved movement often depends on expanded recruitment of premotor, cerebellar, striatal, prefrontal, and cingulo-insular systems involved in motor compensation, effort allocation, and body-state monitoring. Metabolic and pathological studies further indicate energetic vulnerability in demyelinated and chronically injured networks, providing biological plausibility for impaired restoration after repeated signalling demands. These findings support a systems framework in which expanded motor-control recruitment may be compensatory when it preserves performance and remains flexible and recoverable, but may amplify MS fatigue when ordinary activity begins from incompletely restored physiological reserve. We outline testable predictions for identifying a motor-cost fatigue phenotype and for designing repeated-measures studies of activity-related fatigue in MS.
abstract_zh: 摘要 多发性硬化症（MS）疲劳在临床上显而易见，但在机制上尚不清楚。尽管残疾程度轻微、结构性MRI检查稳定或检查时肌力保存，它仍可能主导日常生活。本综述回顾了证据，表明MS疲劳的重要成分可能源于运动控制成本增加以及活动后恢复不全。自愿肌肉激活研究表明，部分MS患者对可用力量的中枢控制不完整，特别是在运动后。功能成像研究表明，看似保持的运动通常依赖于前运动、小脑、纹状体、前额叶及眶缘-岛叶系统的扩展性招募，这些系统参与运动补偿、努力分配和体态监测。代谢和病理学研究进一步指出，脱髓鞘及慢性损伤网络存在能量脆弱性，为重复信号需求后恢复受损提供了生物学合理性。这些发现支持一种系统框架：扩展的运动控制招募在维持表现并保持灵活和可恢复时是补偿性的，但当日常活动始于未完全恢复的生理储备时，它可能放大MS疲劳。我们概述了可检验的预测，用于识别运动成本疲劳表型，并为MS中活动相关疲劳的重复测量研究设计提供依据。
